stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 15 in this context?
stimulus: During a drought, a town limits water use from its reservoir. The equation $V = 15(160 - t)$ models the volume of water $V$, in millions of gallons, left in the reservoir $t$ days after the limits began.
choices: The reservoir held 15 million gallons of water when the limits began.
The reservoir's volume goes down by 15 million gallons each day.
The reservoir's volume goes up by 15 million gallons each day.
The reservoir will run out of water 15 days after the limits began.
explanation: Distribute to get $V = 2{,}400 - 15t$. The coefficient of $t$ is $-15$, so each extra day takes 15 million gallons out of the reservoir. The question asks what the 15 means, and it means the size of that daily drop: the volume falls by 15 million gallons per day.

A.why: You read 15 as the starting amount. The starting volume is the value of $V$ when $t = 0$, which is $15 \cdot 160 = 2{,}400$ million gallons. The 15 is the rate, not the intercept.

C.why: You saw a positive 15 at the front and took it as a gain. Once you distribute, the $t$ term is $-15t$, so the volume falls as time passes.

D.why: You mixed up the two numbers inside the factored form. The reservoir is empty when $160 - t = 0$, so after 160 days, not 15.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 40 in this context?
stimulus: A county clinic runs a flu vaccination campaign using a single shipment of vaccine. The equation $p + 40d = 1{,}200$ relates the number of doses $p$ still in stock to the number of days $d$ since the campaign began.
choices: The clinic gets 40 new doses of vaccine each day of the campaign.
The clinic had 40 doses of vaccine on hand when the campaign began.
The clinic gives out 40 doses of vaccine each day of the campaign.
The clinic's shipment of vaccine runs out 40 days after the campaign began.
explanation: Solve for $p$ to get $p = 1{,}200 - 40d$. The stock begins at 1,200 doses and drops by 40 every day, so 40 is the number of doses the clinic gives out each day. The question asks how much is used, so you give the size of the drop, 40, without the negative sign.

A.why: You saw $+40d$ on the left side and read it as a gain. When you isolate $p$, the term becomes $-40d$, so the stock goes down each day.

B.why: You reported the starting amount when the question was about the rate. At $d = 0$ the stock is $p = 1{,}200$ doses, not 40.

D.why: You treated 40 as the time until the vaccine runs out. Setting $p = 0$ gives $40d = 1{,}200$, so the shipment lasts 30 days.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line in this context?
stimulus: The graph models the number of seabird nesting pairs on an island, $y$, $x$ years after a program to remove rats from the island began.

figure.caption: Seabird Nesting Pairs on the Island
figure.alt: A straight line that rises from left to right, starting at x = 0 and ending at x = 10.

choices: The model predicts an increase of 150 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 35 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 200 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 20 nesting pairs each year.
explanation: Use two clear grid points, $(0, 150)$ and $(10, 350)$. The slope is $\frac{350 - 150}{10 - 0} = \frac{200}{10} = 20$. Since the slope is the change per year, the model predicts 20 more nesting pairs each year.

A.why: You read the y-intercept. 150 is the number of nesting pairs when the program began, not the yearly change.

B.why: You divided the final value by the time, $\frac{350}{10}$, and forgot to subtract the starting 150 first.

C.why: You found the total rise over all 10 years, $350 - 150 = 200$, but didn't divide by the 10 years to get the rate per year.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 50 in this context?
stimulus: A linguist studying early language development models the number of words $W$ that a toddler can say at age $m$ months with the equation $W = 50m - 400$, for $12 \le m \le 30$.
choices: The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 50 words per month.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary is 50 words at age 12 months.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 50 words per year.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 400 words per month.
explanation: 50 is the coefficient of $m$, so it is the rate of change. Its units are words divided by the units of $m$, which is months. Each extra month of age adds about 50 words to the toddler's estimated vocabulary.

B.why: You treated the coefficient as a starting amount. The estimated vocabulary at 12 months is $50(12) - 400 = 200$ words. The 50 is the monthly rate.

C.why: You got the rate right but used the wrong time unit. The input $m$ is measured in months, so the rate is per month, not per year.

D.why: You took the constant term as the rate. The 400 is a fixed adjustment in the model. The rate is the coefficient of $m$.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 40 in this context?
stimulus: At an excavation site, an archaeologist estimates the age $A$, in years, of material found $d$ centimeters below the top of a sediment layer with the equation $A = 1{,}250 + 40d$.
choices: Material at the top of the sediment layer is about 40 years old.
Each extra centimeter of depth adds about 40 years to the age.
Each extra centimeter of depth subtracts about 40 years from the age.
About 40 centimeters of sediment built up at the site each year.
explanation: 40 is the coefficient of $d$, so it is a rate in years per centimeter. For every extra centimeter you dig, the estimated age of the material goes up by about 40 years.

A.why: You reported the rate as the starting value. At the top of the layer, $d = 0$ and $A = 1{,}250$ years. That value is the intercept, not 40.

C.why: You got the sign wrong. The term is $+40d$, so deeper material is older, not younger.

D.why: You turned the rate upside down. 40 years per centimeter means sediment built up at about $\frac{1}{40}$ centimeter per year, not 40 centimeters per year.
